title: Application-send turn shadow policy verification
scope: Verify shadow-only observation, deterministic recommendation, provenance, replay, and force-legacy rollback for application_send_turn_planning. Do not claim a policy winner, active behavior, fairness improvement, latency improvement, or production readiness.
verification_method: Deterministic requirement-home and property tests, focused scheduler and lifecycle correctness tests, allocation and mechanism-cost benchmarks outside correctness CI, permanent local disabled-versus-observe-only and shadow campaigns, schema/checksum validation, and deterministic offline replay.
preconditions: The receive-credit and stream-capacity correctness checkpoint remains preserved.
The application-send force and construction-provenance contract remains green.
All adjacent policy axes are fixed at legacy_current.
The runtime default and applied shadow behavior are legacy_current.
procedure: Validate the new requirement, architecture, work-item, and verification artifacts independently.
Build the relevant projects in Release before testing.
Run deterministic requirement-home tests for disabled, observe-only, shadow, forced, rollback, safe-boundary latch, transition, fallback, and reason precedence.
Run bounded property sequences covering duplicate, delayed, missing, stale, saturated, contradictory, out-of-order, cancellation, disposal, FIN, reset, shutdown, loss, and recovery events.
Run focused scheduler, queue, congestion, pacing, flow-control, ownership, and buffer-limit tests.
Run BenchmarkDotNet mechanism checks only through the nightly or manual performance workflow and retain allocation results.
Run the complete Release correctness suite with Category!=Performance.
Run permanent local disabled-versus-observe-only and shadow replay cells with exact payload and provenance validation.
Validate raw, construction, normalized, curated, and split joins, checksums, exclusions, and axis attribution.
Run deterministic offline replay and prove force-legacy rollback before requesting multi-host shadow review.
expected_result: Every shadow observation produces a versioned deterministic recommendation or conservative fallback with a bounded reason; legacy_current remains applied; no recommendation reaches the scheduler; every forced value retains safety guards; replay is exact; axis provenance and exclusions are append-only; disabled and observe-only paths meet neutrality expectations; and force-legacy rollback restores the null-planner baseline.
status_summary: In progress. The deterministic controller, bounded runtime observe-only and shadow capture, null-planner rollback, separate raw-host evidence stream, closed raw schema, standalone raw-to-epoch conversion, permanent shadow and same-binary disabled-versus-observe-only runner paths, checksum inventory, result/sample/raw-source joins, bounded model-feature transform, axis-specific analysis adapter, focused policy-mechanism benchmarks, immutable ProtocolLab package controls, schema-valid ABBA/BAAB ProtocolLab campaign plans, and explicit Linux ARM64/macOS ARM64 implementation payload support are implemented. The campaign driver is plan-only by default, requires clean committed source for explicit execution, freezes adjacent axes at legacy_current, requests controller-owned isolated-pair placement, records no worker ID, retains returned topology and host rotation evidence, and never authorizes active behavior. Disabled samples require the environment variable to remain unset and reject any axis evidence; observe-only samples require recommendation-free records while both treatments apply legacy_current. One retained local shadow cell produced schema-valid corrected evidence. One same-host disabled-versus-observe-only ABBA cell was correctness-clean but is retained as negative because observe-only p95 exceeded the matched five-percent guardrail. Its 13,570 epochs joined without unmatched epochs; curation retained 4,819 negative rows and preserved 8,751 excluded rows. The leakage audit passed, but one host fingerprint and one workload family honestly produce insufficient_group_diversity and a null rule proposal. Manual BenchmarkDotNet checks reported no managed allocation in the exercised controller and bounded-observation cases; policy-read timing was below reliable resolution and is not claimed. Clean parity-eligible x64 and ARM64 policy packages were built from exact committed source without upload. Release builds, the complete correctness-only Release suite with 9,837 passed and zero failed tests, and focused controller, runtime, rollback, raw-host, schema, conversion, checksum, runner, evidence-join, dataset, analysis-chain, benchmark dry-run, package-template, and campaign-plan tests passed. Broader neutrality, executed multi-host and ARM64 coverage, host and workload holdouts, deterministic offline rule replay, and campaign rollback evidence remain open. No behavior-distinct planner, policy winner, active behavior, or production readiness is claimed.
